scope: Empty spec fields in data/landscape.json (38 chips), excluding price and bill of materials. Entries whose note starts FILL replace an empty value. Entries whose note starts CORRECTION replace a value the row states as unpublished, where a vendor source now publishes it. Values where two allowed sources disagree are in qa/landscape-specs.md, not here.

updates.quote: Rubin’s chip level TDP increases up to 2,300W vs 1000-1400W for Blackwell. ... NVIDIA’s 2300W configuration represents the Max-P configuration, while the efficiency optimized Max-Q configuration runs at 1800W.
updates.note: FILL. Tier B (SemiAnalysis). The article frames Max-P and Max-Q as two power profiles on the same hardware: 'these are not distinct hardware SKUs but the 2 default power profiles'. 2,300 W is the maximum per-GPU setting in the VR NVL72 rack this row describes ('The VR NVL72 system has a TDP up to 220kW for the 2300W Rubin TDP SKU'). Put the 1,800 W Max-Q profile in notes. Nvidia itself still publishes no TDP.

updates.quote: Supporting new data types on MTIA 300 is challenging, especially as models adopt formats with custom scaling, such as row-wise or block-wise scaling for MX4 and NVFP4. While MTIA 300 handles standard hardware-accelerated casts, these emerging types often require specialized scaling that is not natively supported, forcing a fallback to RISC-V execution. ... To address this limitation, we introduced native support for MX4 in MTIA 400.
updates.note: FILL. Tier A. There is no native four-bit datapath; MX4 runs as a RISC-V software fallback. The FP4 cell should read 'not supported'. Update precisionNote to match.
